- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment shifts to bearish.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases when sentiment is bullish; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend if sentiment is trending.
- If sentiment is neutral or declining, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% for each day sentiment drops below 0.50.
- Avoid forecasting price increases when sentiment is bearish and recent price is above 80.00; model tends to overreact; cap at 80.00–82.00 unless sentiment turns bullish.
